lead: D11 detector hand-off: five second-tier revolving-door lobbyists each with $50M+ in 2022-2026 committee-aligned LDA revenue (Richards $84.6M, Lazarski $78.3M, Young $73.3M, Teague $63.9M, O'Neill $62.7M). Verify biographies, current firm affiliation, client rosters, FEC patterns, and identify the strongest say-vs-pay extension for a follow-up data-detective finding.
questions: For each of the 5 lobbyists: confirm current firm, verify covered-position dates, enumerate top current clients, FEC donation pattern.
For each: does a current member of their former committee publicly oppose one of their major clients' interests (say-vs-pay)?
Which of the 5 has the cleanest say-vs-pay extension worthy of promotion to a data-detective finding alongside C-004?

findings.claim: James 'Jim' Richards is a Principal at Cornerstone Government Affairs (since 2005). His pre-Cornerstone roles: Director of Office of Intergovernmental Relations at USDA; appropriations staff for chairs of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, FDA and Related Agencies (Skeen, Bonilla); Chief of Staff to Rep. Steve Pearce (R-NM-2). In 2024 he was the registered lobbyist on 41 active clients, with industry concentration spanning agriculture, defense, technology, higher education and transportation.
findings.evidence: Cornerstone bio: 'Jim Richards joined the firm in 2005 after serving in both the executive and legislative branches of the federal government... Before joining the Cornerstone family, Jim served as the appropriations staff for succeeding chairs of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, FDA and Related Agencies, the Director of the Office of Intergovernmental Relations at the United States Department of Agriculture and the Chief of Staff to his home district Congressman.' His expertise pages explicitly list National Security, Defense & Intelligence, Cyber, Budget & Appropriations, Agriculture. OpenSecrets lobbying summary: 'James Richards is a lobbyist who was hired by 41 client(s) in 2024.'
findings.confidence_rationale: Two independent primary sources: his own firm's bio page and the OpenSecrets LDA-derived profile. Both confirm career arc, current firm, and 2024 client count.

findings.claim: Richards' 2024 client roster at Cornerstone includes Anduril Industries (defense AI startup), Boeing Co, Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Alphabet Inc, Lumen Technologies, iHeartMedia, J&F Investimentos (Brazilian holding co. of JBS — meatpacker), Habematolel Pomo of Upper Lake (tribal client), the National Hockey League, the Cherokee Nation of Oklahoma, the Coalition for Workforce Innovation, CoBank, ChildHelp, City of Cedar Rapids IA, Hunt Development Group, and Fortress Information Security. The 41-client portfolio spans defense procurement (Anduril/Boeing/Kratos), tech-platform regulation (Alphabet), telecom (Lumen), agriculture (J&F), tribal sovereignty, municipal appropriations and others.
findings.evidence: OpenSecrets 2024 client table on his profile lists each pairing as 'Cornerstone Government Affairs | [client name]'. findings.confidence_rationale: Direct LDA-derived OpenSecrets table; client list is a deterministic transform of public Senate LDA filings.

Recipients are exclusively Republican and concentrated on (a) House Republican leadership (Speaker Mike Johnson R-LA at $6,600), (b) House Appropriations Committee leaders (Ken Calvert R-CA, HAC-Defense Chair; Hal Rogers R-KY; Tom Cole R-OK; Mike Simpson R-ID; Robert Aderholt R-AL; Bruce Westerman R-AR; Kay Granger R-TX; John Carter R-TX; Jake Ellzey R-TX), and (c) Senate Republicans (Cruz R-TX $3,500; Barrasso R-WY $6,200; Bernie Moreno R-OH $2,500). findings.claim: Anthony 'Lazer' Lazarski is a Principal at Cornerstone Government Affairs after a 35-year career split between the U.S. Air Force (25 years, retired Colonel) and Capitol Hill (12 years). His most recent congressional role was Senior Advisor to Sen. James Inhofe (R-OK) on national security, foreign affairs, intelligence, veterans affairs, and 'all Department of Defense authorizations and appropriations' (2015-2017 per OpenSecrets; Lazarski's bio describes broader portfolio). Before that he was Professional Staff Member on the Senate Armed Services Committee (2013-2015) overseeing Air Force readiness, Air Force/Navy tactical air programs, military construction, AFRICOM, Defense Working Capital Fund, and Unmanned Aircraft Systems policies. Prior Hill role: Legislative Assistant to Sen. Inhofe (2007-2013). Inhofe was SASC Chairman 2018-2023.
findings.evidence: Cornerstone bio: 'Most recently, Anthony served as the senior advisor to Sen. findings.claim: Jennifer B. Young is co-founder and partner at Tarplin, Downs & Young LLC (founded 2006), a boutique health-policy lobbying firm. Earlier Capitol Hill roles included Senior Health Policy Adviser at House Ways & Means Committee (~2001), Senior Health Policy Adviser at Senate Finance Committee (date unclear), Executive Director of Public Programs at the American Association of Health Plans, and Executive Assistant at the Ohio Department of Human Services. findings.claim: SAY-VS-PAY EXTENSION (Lazarski/Apollo): Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), a sitting member of the Senate Armed Services Committee (Lazarski's former committee), has publicly and in writing attacked both Apollo Global Management specifically AND the entire revolving-door defense lobbyist class that Lazarski exemplifies. Warren co-signed a 2024 letter (with Sen. Ed Markey) demanding accountability from Apollo for its role in the Steward Health Care bankruptcy. Separately, Warren's published 'Reduce Corporate Influence at the Pentagon' platform explicitly attacks the Boeing-Lockheed lobbyist clique: 'These giant contractors have deployed an extremely profitable strategy: recruit armies of lobbyists from former Pentagon officials and congressional staffers who stream through the revolving door... In 2018 alone, the top 20 defense contractors hired 645 former senior government officials, top military brass, Members of Congress, and senior legislative staff as lobbyists.' Lazarski personally is a textbook example: 25-year USAF Colonel + Inhofe SASC staffer + Cornerstone Boeing/GD/Anduril lobbyist. Lazarski lobbies for both Apollo (Warren has attacked) AND Boeing (Warren has attacked). This is a clean two-axis say-vs-pay extension.
findings.evidence: Warren website: 'Warren, Markey Push Apollo Global Management on Role in Steward Health Care's Demise, Call on the Company to Provide Relief from Onerous Leases... "Apollo has had a shadowy role in Steward's leases for years," said Sen. Warren, "Now it is time for Apollo to step into the light".' Warren campaign platform: 'Reduce Corporate Influence at the Pentagon... Let's shut the revolving door between giant contractors and the Pentagon... These giant contractors have deployed an extremely profitable strategy: recruit armies of lobbyists from former Pentagon officials and congressional staffers who stream through the revolving door... I opposed [Boeing's] Shanahan's prior nomination to work as Trump's #2 at DOD because of his lack of foreign policy experience and my concerns about his ability to separate himself from Boeing's financial interests... My plan would ban giant defense contractors from hiring senior DOD officials and general and flag officers for four years after they leave the Department.' Confirming clients: Lazarski's 2024 LDA filings include 'Cornerstone Government Affairs | Apollo Global Management' AND 'Cornerstone Government Affairs | Boeing Co' AND 'Cornerstone Government Affairs | General Dynamics'.
findings.confidence_rationale: Three independent primary sources establish: (a) Lazarski actively lobbies for Apollo and Boeing on behalf of Cornerstone, (b) Warren has named Apollo by name in formal Senate correspondence demanding accountability for healthcare collapse caused by PE financial engineering, (c) Warren has published a campaign-platform document explicitly targeting the revolving-door defense-contractor lobbyist class. The two attack lines (Apollo as bad-actor PE landlord; Boeing-Lockheed-style defense contractors as lobbying-corruption avatars) both hit Lazarski's client mix.

findings.claim: FIRM-LEVEL OBSERVATION: Three of the five top-tier lobbyists work at the same firm — Cornerstone Government Affairs (Richards $84.6M; Lazarski $78.3M). Cornerstone is therefore the dominant employer in the second tier behind Brownstein Hyatt's #1 status (which holds the C-004 cluster). At a minimum: Richards and Lazarski share office space, client overlap (both list Cherokee Nation of Oklahoma, Anduril, Fortress Information Security, Boeing-adjacent defense work, J&F Investimentos-adjacent agriculture work). Cornerstone's revolving-door personnel count (per OpenSecrets) is 66 — meaning it has accumulated dozens of ex-Hill staffers comparable to Richards and Lazarski. The firm should be examined as an entity in addition to its individual lobbyists.
findings.evidence: Cornerstone bios for both individuals identify them as Principals at the same Washington DC office (800 Maine Avenue, SW, 7th Floor).
